segments.text: Lesson 47
segments.translation: 第47课

segments.text: Too high a price?
segments.translation: 代价太高了吗？

segments.text: Listen to the tape then answer this question.
segments.translation: 听录音，然后回答问题。

segments.text: What does the writer describe as an 'amusing old-fashioned source of noise' ?
segments.translation: 作者把什么描述为一种“有趣的老式噪音源”？

segments.text: Pollution is the price we pay for an overpopulated, overindustrialized planet.
segments.translation: 污染是我们为一个人口过剩、过度工业化的星球所付出的代价。

segments.text: When you come to think about it, there are only four ways you can deal with rubbish:
segments.translation: 当你仔细想想时，处理垃圾的方法只有4种：

segments.text: dump it, burn it, turn it into something you can use again, attempt to produce less of it.
segments.translation: 倾倒、焚烧、将其转化为可以再次使用的东西、或者尝试减少垃圾的产生。

segments.text: We keep trying all four methods, but sheer volume of rubbish we produce worldwide threatens to overwhelm us.
segments.translation: 我们不断尝试这4种方法，但我们在全球范围内产生的大量垃圾威胁着要淹没我们。

segments.text: Rubbish, however, is only part of the problem of polluting our planet.
segments.translation: 然而，垃圾只是污染我们星球的一部分问题。

segments.text: The need to produce ever increasing quantities of cheap food leads to a different kind of pollution.
segments.translation: 生产不断增加的廉价食品的需求导致了另一种污染。

segments.text: Industriallized farming metheods produce cheap meat products: beef, pork and chicken.
segments.translation: 工业化的耕作方法生产出廉价的肉制品：牛肉、猪肉和鸡肉。

segments.text: The use of pesticides and fertilizers produces cheap grain and vegetables.
segments.translation: 杀虫剂和化肥的使用生产出廉价的谷物和蔬菜。

segments.text: The price we pay for cheap food may be already too high:
segments.translation: 我们为廉价食品付出的代价可能已经太高了：

segments.text: Mad Cow Disease (BSE) in cattle, salmonella in chicken and eggs, and listeria in dairy products.
segments.translation: 牛群中的疯牛病、鸡肉和鸡蛋中的沙门氏菌，以及奶制品中的李斯特菌。

segments.text: And if you think you'll abandon meat and become a vegetarian,
segments.translation: 如果你打算放弃吃肉而成为一名素食者，

segments.text: you have the choice of very expensive organically-grown vegetables
segments.translation: 你面临的选择是：要么选择非常昂贵的有机种植蔬菜，

segments.text: or a steady diet of pesticides every time you think you're eating fresh salads and vegetables,
segments.translation: 要么每次当你以为自己在吃新鲜沙律和蔬菜，

segments.text: or just having an innocent glass of water!
segments.translation: 或者只是喝一杯纯净的水时，实际上是在摄入杀虫剂。

segments.text: However, there is an even more insidious kind of pollution that particularly affects urban area and invades our daily lives, and that is noise.
segments.translation: 然而，有一种甚至更隐蔽的污染特别影响城市地区并侵入我们的日常生活，那就是噪音。

segments.text: Burglar alarms going off at any time of the day or night serve only to annoy passers-by and actually assist burglars to burgle.
segments.translation: 在白天或晚上的任何时间响起的防盗警报器，只会令路人感到厌烦，而实际上却在协助窃贼行窃。

segments.text: Car alarms constantly scream at us in the street and are a source of profound irritation.
segments.translation: 汽车警报器在街道上不停地对着我们尖叫，是极度恼火的根源。

segments.text: A recent survey of the effects of noise revealed (surprisingly?)
segments.translation: 最近一项关于噪音影响的调查显示（令人惊讶吗？），

segments.text: that dogs barking incessantly in the night rated the highest form of noise pollution on a scale ranging from 1 to 7.
segments.translation: 在1到7级的范围内，夜间犬吠被评为最高等级的噪音污染。

segments.text: The survey revealed a large number of sources of noise that we really dislike.
segments.translation: 调查显示了大量我们真正厌恶的噪音源。

segments.text: Lawn mowers whining on a summer's day, late-night parties in apartment blocks,
segments.translation: 夏日里的割草机轰鸣声、公寓楼里的深夜聚会、

segments.text: noisy neighbours, vehicles of all kinds,
segments.translation: 嘈杂的邻居、各种车辆、

segments.text: especially large container trucks thundering through quiet villages,
segments.translation: 特别是轰隆隆穿过宁静村庄的大型集装箱卡车、

segments.text: planes and helicopters flying overhead, large radios carried round in public places and played at maximum volume.
segments.translation: 飞过头顶的飞机和直升机，以及在公共场所携带并以最大音量播放的大型收音机。

segments.text: New technology has also made its own contribution to noise.
segments.translation: 新技术也对噪音做出了自己的“贡献”。

segments.text: A lot of people object to mobile phones, especially when they are used in public places like restaurant or on public transport.
segments.translation: 许多人反对使用手机，特别是当它们在餐厅或公共交通工具等公共场所使用时。

segments.text: Loud conversations on mobile phones invade our thoughts or interrupt the pleasure of meeting friends for a quiet chat.
segments.translation: 用手机大声交谈会侵入我们的思绪，或中断与朋友静静聊天的乐趣。

segments.text: The noise pollution survey revealed a rather surprising and possibly amusing old-fashioned source of noise.
segments.translation: 噪音污染调查显示了一个相当令人惊讶，可能还很有趣的老式噪音源。

segments.text: It turned out to be snoring! Men were found to be the worst offenders.
segments.translation: 那竟然是打呼噜！结果发现男人是最大的肇事者。

segments.text: It was revealed that 20% of men in their mid-thirties snore.
segments.translation: 据透露，在30多岁的男人中，有20%的人打呼噜。

segments.text: This figure rises to a staggering 60% of men in their sixties.
segments.translation: 这一数字在60多岁的男人中上升到了惊人的60%。

segments.text: Against these figures, it was found that only 5% of women snore regularly,
segments.translation: 相比之下，只有5%的女性经常打呼噜，

segments.text: while the rest are constantly woken or kept awake by their trumpeting partners.
segments.translation: 而其余的人则经常被她们那像吹喇叭一样的伴侣吵醒或吵得睡不着。

words.meaning: 大声地宣扬(此处指大声打鼾)

segments.text: Whatever the source of noise, one thing is certain: silence, it seems, has become a golden memory.
segments.translation: 不论噪音源于何处，有一点是肯定的：沉默似乎已成为一段美好的回忆。
